title: Ask the Critical Question
hook: A particulate sensor alert flashes beside an inspection report draft. One question decides whether a cue deserves you.
counterintuition: The easy mistake is to treat all alerts as bad instead of judging each cue against prior intent and real obligations. The sharper move is to interrogate each external cue by asking whether it serves the thing you meant to do right now.
tryThisNow: When the next cue arrives, ask whether it moves the scheduled block forward; answer yes, no, or real obligation before acting.
keyTakeaway: Interrogate each external cue by asking whether it serves the thing you meant to do right now so prior intent beats the nearest convincing escape.

breakdown.fastRead: A field alert flashes on an air-quality tablet. The cue feels important because it is loud, not because it serves the next task. A cue earns attention only when it serves the chosen work.
